title: A semiabelian group extension by Gm reflects ampleness
statement: Let $S$ be a normal integral Noetherian affine scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], where Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact, and normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains. A commutative $S$-group scheme has addition, inverse and identity as $S$-morphisms satisfying the commutative group identities [def-sc-group-scheme, def-pc-fibre-product]; separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $E$ and $H$ be smooth separated commutative $S$-group schemes of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], both with semiabelian geometric fibres [def-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-fibres]. Suppose $q:E\to H$ is an $S$-group homomorphism, faithfully flat of finite presentation [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism], and an embedding $j:\mathbf G_{m,S}\to E$ identifies $\mathbf G_{m,S}=\operatorname{Spec}_S\mathcal O_S[t,t^{-1}]$ [def-sc-gm-ga] with its scheme-theoretic kernel. Assume $1\to\mathbf G_{m,S}\xrightarrow{j}E\xrightarrow{q}H\to1$ is exact as fppf sheaves [def-pc-fppf-site]; equivalently $q$ is the group quotient torsor with $E\times_S\mathbf G_{m,S}\simeq E\times_HE$, $(u,a)\mapsto(u,u+j(a))$. Let $M$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_H$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Assume $M$ is symmetric under the group inversion $\iota_H=[-1]_H$: there is an isomorphism $\iota_H^*M\simeq M$. If the tensor pullback $q^*M$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is ample on $E$, then $M$ is ample on $H$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. This is absolute ampleness over the specified affine base. No cubical structure, inversion-norm hypothesis or properness of $H$ is assumed; inversion symmetry of $M$ is essential in this corrected relative formulation. The homomorphism and group-extension hypotheses are essential; this is not a descent assertion for arbitrary $\mathbf G_m$-torsors.

source.place: XI 1.11, ampleness comparison for group quotients: supporting source for the field abelian-quotient case. The relative semiabelian Gm-extension assertion here is an agent-formulated geometric prerequisite, not claimed as the verbatim statement of XI 1.11. Original and proof of this relative formulation WANTED. No general fpqc descent of absolute ampleness is asserted.

proof.text: Finite presentation implies finite type directly from its affine finite-polynomial presentation and quasi-compactness. Hence $E$ and $H$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Their geometric fibres are connected: use the supplied semiabelian presentation and [lem-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-power-integrality] with $n=1$; smoothness and finite type of these fibres follow from [lem-pc-proper-base-change] and [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. The algebraic-closure connectedness criterion then makes every residue-field fibre geometrically connected. Since $S$ is normal integral and $E,H$ have identities, [lem-sbc-smooth-connected-generic-geometry] makes their local rings integrally closed domains. In particular the normality and finite-type hypotheses for the eigensection-chart input hold for $E$. The separatedness of geometric fibres is preserved by base change. Writing $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, its affine coordinate ring is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth].

source.place: Agent assembly; ideal-section and nonvanishing-locus arguments, with the named DAG inputs.

proof.text: Write $T=\mathbf G_{m,S}$ and let it act on $E$ by $a(t,u)=u+j(t)$. The torsor identity $q a=q p_2$ gives $L=q^*M$ its canonical $T$-linearization; the unit and cocycle equalities are the identity on the common pullback from $H$. Choose the assumed isomorphism $\iota_H^*M\simeq M$. Because $q\iota_E=\iota_Hq$, it induces $\iota_E^*L\simeq L$, and hence identifications for every positive power. These identifications are compatible with the canonical pullback linearizations when inversion sends $t$ to $t^{-1}$: both sides are pullbacks of the chosen sheaf map on $H$. Tensor-power and composite-pullback identifications are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor].

source.place: Agent assembly; ideal-section and nonvanishing-locus arguments, with the named DAG inputs.

proof.text: Fix $s\in S$ and its identity point $e_E(s)$. Apply [lem-sfb-linearized-ample-eigen-affine-cover] to the ample linearized $L$ on $E$ to obtain $n\geq1$, a weight $w$, and $\sigma\in\Gamma(E,L^{\otimes n})$ whose affine nonvanishing open $U$ contains $e_E(s)$. Transfer $\iota_E^*\sigma$ through the preceding isomorphism and call it $\tau$. Its weight is $-w$: substitute $\iota_E(tu)=t^{-1}\iota_E(u)$ into the displayed eigensection identity of that node and pull back the chosen sheaf map from $H$. Thus $\rho=\sigma\otimes\tau$ has weight zero for every test algebra, as the factors $t^w$ and $t^{-w}$ cancel. Its nonvanishing locus is $W=U\cap\iota_E^{-1}(U)$ by the residue-field tensor formula. It contains $e_E(s)$ and is affine: it is the nonvanishing locus of $\tau|_U$ on affine $U$, so [lem-sc-affine-cap-section-open] applies.

source.place: Agent assembly; ideal-section and nonvanishing-locus arguments, with the named DAG inputs.

proof.text: The fppf cover $q$ is fpqc by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc]. The weight-zero identity for $\rho$, under $E\times_HE\simeq E\times_ST$, is precisely equality of its two pullbacks to $E\times_HE$ using the canonical descent identifications of $q^*(M^{\otimes2n})$. Full faithfulness of [lem-pc-fpqc-descent], applied to the map $\mathcal O_E\to q^*(M^{\otimes2n})$ defined by $\rho$, gives a section $v\in\Gamma(H,M^{\otimes2n})$ whose pullback is $\rho$. The residue-field formula in [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] gives $q^{-1}(H_v)=W$. No assertion of fpqc descent of ampleness is used.

source.place: Agent assembly; ideal-section and nonvanishing-locus arguments, with the named DAG inputs.

proof.text: The affine open $W$ is a finite-type $S$-scheme: $E$ is Noetherian, so every intersection of its opens is quasi-compact; its open inclusion is therefore quasi-compact and of finite type, and compose with $E\to S$. The restricted $T$-action is free on all test schemes by the original torsor isomorphism. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-free-split-torus-invariants] to $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ over $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$. It says that its fppf orbit sheaf is $\operatorname{Spec}(B^T)$. This orbit sheaf is also $H_v$: any test map to $H_v$ lifts fppf locally to $W$ by base change of $q$, and any two lifts differ by a unique element of $T$. These local descriptions and fppf sheafification give mutually inverse maps of represented sheaves; Yoneda gives $H_v\simeq\operatorname{Spec}(B^T)$. Thus $H_v$ is affine and meets the fibre above $s$.

source.place: Agent assembly; ideal-section and nonvanishing-locus arguments, with the named DAG inputs.

proof.text: The image $V=p(H_v)$ in $S$ is open, since $p:H\to S$ is smooth, hence flat and locally of finite presentation, and such maps are open. It contains $s$ because $\rho(e_E(s))\ne0$. Choose a principal affine neighbourhood $S_s=D(f)\subseteq V$ of $s$ in the affine base $S$. The nonvanishing locus of $v|_{H_{S_s}}$ is $H_v\times_SS_s$, a principal open in the affine $H_v$, hence affine. It meets every fibre over $S_s$ by the definition of $V$. On $H_{S_s}\to S_s$, smoothness, separatedness and finite presentation persist by base change, and the connected-fibre conclusion of step 1 persists. The affine base $S_s$ is locally Noetherian and normal because its local rings are local rings of $S$. Therefore [lem-sfb-group-affine-section-ampleness] applied to $M|_{H_{S_s}}$, exponent $2n\geq1$ and section $v$ proves absolute ampleness on $H_{S_s}$.

source.place: Agent assembly; ideal-section and nonvanishing-locus arguments, with the named DAG inputs.

proof.text: As $s$ varies, these principal affine opens $S_s$ cover $S$. The morphism $H\to S$ is quasi-compact by finite presentation. Apply [lem-trf-scheme-relative-ample-affine-cover] with this affine open covering and the restrictions shown ample in step 6. Taking its affine open $V=S$ gives that $M$ is ample on the whole of $H$. This proves the corrected symmetric relative assertion. It does not supply the unsymmetric input requested by the parent norm-reflection proof.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q134-bb82b6f55 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: E7 statement correction accepted. The base item (any M with q*M ample implies M ample) is false. Kallal arXiv:2610.26133v1 §4.1, read online: over R=C[[q1,q2]] with Tate parameter q1q2 and ψ(y)=q1^{(y²+y)/2}q2^{(y²−y)/2}, there is a line P that is ample on the generic fibre but not on G. I checked the bimultiplicativity (q1q2)^{y1y2}. The frame extension E=(P⊗(ι*P)^∨)^× → G has semiabelian fibres (closed fibre: an extension of G_m by G_m). Then q*(P²)≅q*(P⊗ι*P) is ample: the norm is symmetric and generically ample (Moret-Bailly VI 3.1), and q is affine. But P² is not ample. The delivery adds only ι_H^*M≅M and names the change in the report. Steps checked against the full cited statements: (1) Noetherian, integral geometric fibres via power-integrality with n=1, geometric connectedness, normality via sbc-smooth-connected-generic-geometry; (2) canonical linearization and symmetry pulled back from H; (3) the new chart node gives σ of weight w, τ=φ(ι*σ) has weight −w (checked by hand), W=U∩ι^{-1}U is affine by the cap lemma; (4) weight 0 equals descent compatibility, and fpqc full faithfulness gives v with q^{-1}H_v=W; (5) the action on W is free and of finite type, affine-free-split-torus-invariants plus torsor base change plus Yoneda give H_v affine; (6) flat lfp open image, principal D(f), then group-affine-section-ampleness, all hypotheses checked; (7) 01VJ affine-cover gluing. New node lem-sfb-linearized-ample-eigen-affine-cover: statement only, self-contained, true. Argument: invariant affine U, a section vanishing on the reduced invariant complement, weight components vanish on Z by Laurent base change, cap lemma. It is general and strictly smaller than the item. No duplicate found (GIT/PGL linearization nodes, invariant-affines and coaction nodes all lack it). Batch-5 flags: smooth-composition (Mathlib-level), fppf-is-fpqc and relative-ample-affine-cover (sk-i-curve-zero foundations, 022C/01VJ), def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space (a definition), fppf-covering-base-change (Mathlib), and the Proj twist comparison: all generic, none a trace-formula or Poincaré-duality step, so accepted. The tool_uses of generic scheme and descent nodes are accepted. No SGA source is used.
